title: Brooklyn, Massachusetts: Sewer Camera Inspection, Storm/Sanitary Separation, and PVC Drain Retrofit for a 1957 Addition

locations.name: Brooklyn, Massachusetts
locations.basis: Transcript states the site is in Brooklyn, Massachusetts.

summary: This This Old House Live segment follows Kevin and Richard as they work on a heavily renovated Brooklyn, MA home addition that connects to a municipal water and sewer system. The hosts describe the three main utilities entering the property (water supply, sanitary sewer, and storm sewer) and clarify ownership boundaries between homeowner and city, including the shut-off valve location and the responsibility line for storm drainage. The interior plan features new PVC drain lines under a slab, a future master bathroom vent and trap, and a camera inspection of the sewer line that reveals dirt buildup, a transition to orangeburg/clay pipe with root intrusion, and a sag in the town sewer. The team discusses repair options (open-cut replacement with PVC versus liner options), the cost implications of digging versus piping lining, and the need for a bonded contractor when cutting into street/sidewalk. They also cover drainage philosophy (keeping water outside the building, proper pitch and rise), and the permitting process that can impact schedule. All of this is conveyed through live Q&A and visual demonstrations using an in-camera feed on an iPad during the workflow.
